title: This Paradoxical Desert Landscape Is Filled with Fresh Water
author: David Nield
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementEnvironmentThis Paradoxical Desert Landscape Is Filled with Fresh WaterDunes and lakes as far as the eye can seeDNBy David Nield3:00 PM CDT on August 7, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleTo fully appreciate the spectacular contradictions of Lençóis Maranhenses National Park in northeastern Brazil, you really need to see them from above—namely, from images taken by the NASA Landsat 9 satellite.Subscribe to skip adsFeatured VideoPowered By 10 Centuries-Old Quakes May Drive Much of North America’s Seismic ActivityShareNextStayWhat makes the region such a paradox, as these shots show, is that it mixes vast sandy dunes with an astounding number of freshwater lagoons. Basically, it’s a desert with an oasis everywhere you turn.COMPLEX ECOSYSTEM: The dunes in Lençóis Maranhenses National Park, which you can see in the tan section of this photo, are surrounded by ocean and forests. Within the dunes, the many lagoons can be seen as a subtle pattern of what look like blue specks in the tan. Image by NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison.Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
